bib.title: Text Analytics with Python, Chapter 4: Text Classification

question: How is text classification formulated as supervised ML, and how do you build and evaluate a multi-class text classifier end to end with BoW, TF-IDF and word2vec features?
contributions: Formal definition of text classification and the train/predict blueprint
From-scratch BoW, TF-IDF and (TF-IDF weighted) averaged word2vec feature extractors
Multinomial NB and SVM overview; accuracy/precision/recall/F1 worked example
20-class 20 Newsgroups case study with six models and error analysis

method.summary: Book chapter with a 20 Newsgroups case study: normalise, extract BoW/TF-IDF/averaged-word2vec features, fit MultinomialNB and hinge-loss SGD SVM, evaluate on a 33% test split.

datasets.name: 20 Newsgroups
datasets.preprocessing: drop empty docs; expand contractions, POS-aware lemmatise, strip punctuation, remove NLTK stopwords

baselines: MNB vs SVM; BoW vs TF-IDF vs averaged word2vec vs TF-IDF weighted word2vec
eval.protocol: single split, no CV, no tuning

availability.code: normalization.py, feature_extractors.py, feature_extraction_demo.py in chapter code files

results.claim: Book states ensemble methods (random forests, gradient boosting) often perform poorly on text because they overfit; no experiment given
results.setup: asserted in the classification algorithms section, not tested
results.quote: because they are very prone to overfitting

limits: Hyperparameter tuning is explicitly not done: 'the models we will be building work well with default hyperparameter configurations'.
Single train/test split, no cross-validation, no seeds or variance, no timing; only MNB and SGD hinge SVM compared (no logistic regression, trees or boosting experiments).
Code is Python 2 (print statements), sklearn.cross_validation, gensim size=, SGDClassifier n_iter, pattern.en: dated.
Text says test set is 30 percent and passes test_data_proportion=0.3, but prepare_datasets ignores it and uses test_size=0.33.
word2vec trained on the training split only with size=500, window=100, min_count=30; no pretrained vectors or contextual models.
No justification for dense features losing beyond reporting the numbers.
practices: Remove headers, footers and quotes from 20 Newsgroups so the model does not overfit to email addresses or headers (p.204).
Apply identical normalisation and feature extraction in training and prediction; fit the vectoriser on training data only and reuse it on new documents (p.173, p.181).
Never tune against the holdout test set; tune on validation or cross-validation (p.194).
Inspect misclassified documents and the confusion matrix, then adjust feature extraction (p.211-214).
Multinomial NB takes non-negative features: counts or TF-IDF both work (p.196).
Be careful with random forests and gradient boosting on text (p.195).

terms.definition: the process of assigning text documents into one or more classes or categories, assuming that we have a predefined set of classes
priorities or weights are given to specific subjects or topics in the text content that would help determine the class of the document
influenced by user requests and is targeted towards specific user groups and audiences
two classes; more than two classes with one prediction each; more than one predicted class per data point
a mathematical and algebraic model for transforming and representing text documents as numeric vectors of specific terms that form the vector dimensions
idf(t) = 1 + log(C / (1 + df(t))) style smoothing with an imaginary document containing every term; tfidf rows L2-normalised
sum of in-vocabulary word vectors divided by the number of matched words
each matched word vector weighted by its TF-IDF, summed, and divided by the sum of the weights
alpha=1 is Laplace smoothing and alpha<1 is Lidstone smoothing for multinomial NB
max(0, 1 - y_i(w.x_i + b)); gives soft-margin SVM; used by sklearn SVC, LinearSVC, SGDClassifier(loss='hinge')
